rows.what_the_ink_shows: The slanted margin note says Comparer CF [Roman numeral] p.46 ff. et aussi p.27 ff. After rotating the note, three separate I strokes follow the initial glyph, the last close to the top page edge. The first glyph includes a left descending stem and rising right arm compatible with V, but a strong crossing/overwritten diagonal remains; it does not securely exclude X. Viewed crops/156-9_scan130_L1105.jpg [180,0,340,163] and crops/156-9_scan130_L1105_context.jpg [17,0,346,601], both rotated 52 degrees clockwise after contrast 1.6 and enlarged to 3200 pixels across.
rows.note: L1105.R1: Replace the original XIII|XII doubt with VIII|XIII: the three trailing I strokes are visible, while the overwritten initial V/X is not secure enough for an unqualified VIII. Preserve both overline and underline macros around the numeral. The row's identification of the intended reference with 156-8 pp.46 and27 is supplied background only; those scans were not consulted and that argument does not override the crossed ink. The main reader inspected the rotated numeral and accepted VIII|XIII as the final optical uncertainty; no unqualified numeral is adopted.

events.type: used and rechecked in this run
events.outcome: Viewed the full assigned scan and both enlarged rotated crops, compared the original numeral uncertainty, and proposed VIII|XIII to record the visible three trailing I strokes and unresolved V/X overwrite. No claim is made that the intended fascicule is proved by page references.
